title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

relationships.phenotype: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the dystonin gene (DST).

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the dystonin gene (DST).
checks.evidence_quote: We now report an inherited skin fragility disorder with a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST)
checks.explanation: The abstract reports only a homozygous mutation. It does not mention compound heterozygous mutations.

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3 (EBS3) is an autosomal recessive skin fragility disorder. Patients have trauma-induced blisters and erosions, mainly around the ankles and feet. The disorder is caused by loss of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen-1 (BPAG1-e, also known as BP230), which is encoded by the DST gene. Skin from affected individuals shows loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and no immunostaining for BPAG1-e (Groves et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2012; Ganani et al., 2021).

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3 (EBS3) is an autosomal recessive skin fragility disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: the clinicopathological findings expand the molecular basis of EB by identifying BPAG1-e pathology in a new form of autosomal recessive EB simplex
checks.explanation: The abstract calls it an inherited skin fragility disorder and a new autosomal recessive form of EB simplex.

checks.claim: Patients with EBS3 have trauma-induced blisters and erosions, mainly around the ankles and feet.
checks.evidence_quote: The affected individuals had a lifelong history of trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles, feet, hands and elbows (Groves et al.; Liu et al [*].).
checks.explanation: Second-hand: the evidence is a paragraph of Walko et al. (2015) (PMID 26017636) describing PMID 22113475, not the paper's own text; the claim was not checked against PMID 22113475 itself. Verdict on the later paper's description: supported. Second-hand description (Walko 2015); also lists hands and elbows.

checks.evidence_quote: The mutation, p.Gln1124X, leads to the loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and a complete absence of skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e
checks.explanation: The abstract attributes the disorder to a nonsense mutation that causes complete absence of BPAG1-e (BP230).

checks.evidence_quote: dystonin gene (DST) that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1, BPAG1-e (also known as BP230)
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) reported a 38-year-old man from a Kuwaiti family. He had lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles. From age 37 years he had episodic numbness in his limbs. Groves et al. (2010) noted that these neurologic symptoms might also be due to the DST mutation. However, the patient also had a diagnosis of CADASIL, a cerebral small-vessel arteriopathy, which complicated the genotype-phenotype interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Ganani et al. (2021) reported 5 patients with EBS from 3 families. Ganani et al. (2021) also reviewed 6 previously reported cases, bringing the total number of individuals with EBS due to DST variants to 11. They observed that patients had distinctive phenotypes regardless of the causative variant.

paragraphs.text: In a 38-year-old Kuwaiti man with EBS3, Groves et al. (2010) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the DST gene, gln1124-to-ter (Q1124X). The mutation lies in the region encoding the coiled-coil domain of BPAG1-e. Transmission electron microscopy had shown complete loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques. Immunofluorescence microscopy with antibodies to hemidesmosomal inner plaque components showed complete absence of BP230 staining.

paragraphs.text: Ganani et al. (2021) used whole-exome and direct sequencing to identify biallelic DST mutations in 5 patients with EBS from 3 families. The mutations included a novel 1-bp duplication, c.7097dupA, which results in a tyr2366-to-ter (Y2366X) substitution, and a second novel mutation, a 1-bp deletion (c.7429delC) that results in a frameshift (Leu2477SerfsTer13).
